paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in Acts 14. In Iconium a great number believe, then comes a plan to stone Paul and Barnabas, so they flee to Lystra, where the crowds want to sacrifice to them and then Paul gets stoned (Acts 14:1-19). That is a ROLLER COASTER, and they stayed on it. The lesson isn't that serving God gets you applause or that it gets you rocks, but that the work goes on through both.

Look at what they tell the disciples on the way back: "We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God," (Acts 14:22). They didn't say that from a comfy chair. Paul had just gotten up and gone back into the city after being dragged out of it (Acts 14:19-20). Hardship doesn't mean you've lost the road, friend. And when the crowd wanted to treat them like gods, they tore their clothes and pointed to the living God instead (Acts 14:14-15). Whether people throw stones or flowers, the glory goes to Him.

The best part is the ending. They gather the church and report "all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles" (Acts 14:27). Notice who gets the credit. Not Paul, not Barnabas, God. So when your own week gets bumpy, baker, keep baking, keep your eyes on Him, and keep telling people what He did. This story is not over, and neither is the teaching.
